curriculum.lesson_evidence: Rules make games safe and fair. Fair play means following the rules, taking turns, including others and being honest. Sportsmanship means showing respect when winning or losing: saying 'good game', accepting referee decisions, shaking hands where that is comfortable and encouraging teammates. Everyone, including referees and opponents, deserves respect.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A player steps out of bounds before scoring, but the referee did not see it. What is the fair play choice, and what would a good sport say to the other team after losing?

FEEDBACK
Fair play: tell the referee so the point is not counted. After losing, a good sport says, 'Good game' and may shake hands. Honest play matters more than winning.

WATCH FOR
Believing winning is the only goal of sport. Fair play, effort and respect matter at least as much as the score.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Write a Sports Code of Conduct with six rules for players, spectators and officials. For each rule, write a good example and a poor example. Add how a good sport responds to a loss and to a win.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

WORKED MODEL

TRY FIRST
A player steps out of bounds before scoring, but the referee did not see it. What is the fair play choice, and what would a good sport say to the other team after losing?

FEEDBACK
Fair play: tell the referee so the point is not counted. After losing, a good sport says, 'Good game' and may shake hands. Honest play matters more than winning.

Everyone, including referees and opponents, deserves respect.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
